prompt: A frame from a 35mm feature film, full-bleed: Chicago, 1928, a low-ceilinged speakeasy club in a brick basement, sawdust on the floor, spilled gin glinting on a scarred bar. The camera lies on the floor beside the bass drum, looking up through the legs of the band, gangsters in pinstripes with a battered trumpet and a banjo, at three people dancing arm in arm in the middle: the mayor, a tall, skinny man in a bowler hat with a heavy gold chain of office round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks, a pencil-thin grey moustache, between the red leader, a ginger man with mutton-chop whiskers and a red carnation, and the blue leader, a woman with a black bob and a blue carnation, all three laughing. Behind the band, a hand-cranked lantern projector throws oil and dye squeezed between two hot glass plates, so slow bubbling blooms of magenta, emerald and orange crawl across the bricks, the dancers' faces and the low plank ceiling. Through the gaps in those ceiling boards, thin blades of lamplight from the street above flicker with the shadows of stamping, fighting feet, and dust sifts down onto the dancers. The frame is canted. No lettering anywhere.
